title: Protecting the Public
whatItIs: Construction work kills and injures people who aren't part of it, including children. Sites must keep the public out and keep the risks inside the perimeter.

keyFacts.text: Employers MUST run their work so that people they don't employ aren't put at risk, so far as reasonably practicable.
A contractor MUST NOT start work until reasonable steps are taken to keep unauthorised people off site.

keyFacts: A 2 m high fence that's hard to climb is an effective barrier for most sites.
Plan deliveries to avoid busy times for pedestrians, such as the school run.
Barriers should preferably be at least 1 m back from the edge of an excavation.

items.title: Perimeter
items.text: Close-mesh fence, gates locked when the site is empty.

items.title: Visitors
items.text: Report in, get information and PPE; escorted if needed.

items.title: Out of hours
items.text: Remove ladders, immobilise plant, lower buckets and forks.

items.title: Excavations
items.text: Barriers or covers; backfill soon; don't pile spoil on pavements.

items.title: Falling objects
items.text: Double-board platforms; fans, crash decks or tunnels.

items.title: Children
items.text: Sites attract them. Liaise with schools; brief drivers.

a.label: Escorted visitor
points: Told the main hazards and controls

b.label: Unescorted visitor
points: Must know the site and its risks

onTheTest.question: Work stops for the day. What should happen to ladders on the scaffold?
options: Remove them and lock them away
Leave them tied in for the morning
Lay them flat on the platform
onTheTest.why: HSG151: out of hours, remove ladders from the scaffold and secure them in a compound or storage container, so children and others can't climb up.

onTheTest.question: A passer-by is hit by debris from your scaffold and taken to hospital for treatment. Must this be reported?
options: Only if they stay in overnight
Only if they're off work 7 days
onTheTest.why: RIDDOR reg 5: an injury to a person not at work must be reported if they're taken from the scene of the accident to hospital for treatment.

traps: Children see sites as playgrounds: if people can still get in, add more measures.
Don't pile materials or spoil on pavements, forcing pedestrians into the road.
Lock away cartridge tools and clear up used and misfired cartridges at least daily.

sources.doc: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974
HSE L153 Managing health and safety in construction (CDM 2015)
